summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.50/2300)

data.turoyo: I arʕo dəwriwola w kərwiwola w ṯunanwola w bəṯər zərʕiwola warzo.
data.translation: They would plough the land and break it up and plough it a second time, and afterwards sow it as a melon field.

rationale: First Infectum-wa box after round 1, with explicit land theme and suffixes shared across cultivation stages. Translation is project machine translation.

data.turoyo: Kkoru i arʕo, qamayto, bəṯr kmo yawme d mkaməl a ḥrene krowo kṯunelən, bəṯr mu ṯnoyano kəmbasamme, bəṯr mu bəsomano gzuraʕʕe.
data.translation: Zunächst führt er (auf) dem Acker das erste Pflügen durch, nach ein paar Tagen, wenn er auch bei den anderen das erste Pflügen durchgeführt hat, führt er das zweite Pflügen durch, und nach dem zweiten Pflügen das feine Pflügen. Nach dem feinen Pflügen besät er (die Felder).

rationale: Thin Infectum 1; explicit field object and the sequence distinguishing first, second and fine ploughing.

data.turoyo: Kkoru i arʕo, qamayto, bəṯr kmo yawme d mkaməl a ḥrene krowo kṯunelən, bəṯr mu ṯnoyano kəmbasamme, bəṯr mu bəsomano gzuraʕʕe.
data.translation: Zunächst führt er (auf) dem Acker das erste Pflügen durch, nach ein paar Tagen, wenn er auch bei den anderen das erste Pflügen durchgeführt hat, führt er das zweite Pflügen durch, und nach dem zweiten Pflügen das feine Pflügen. Nach dem feinen Pflügen besät er (die Felder).

rationale: Thin Infinitiv 1; replaces an isolated dictionary form as sole contextual evidence, with krowo complement of finish.

data.turoyo: W kkurwənne w ṯunanne w mbasmənne w zurʕənne warzo, lašan d miḥafəḏ̣ u karmo, d zrəʕʕe u ḥaṯo, w lašan d uṯalle hatən mi arʕo, d lə fayšo xliṯo.
data.translation: Dann führen sie das erste, zweite und dritte Pflügen durch und säen auf den Äckern Melonen ein, damit der neue Weinberg, den sie angelegt haben, geschützt ist, und damit sie von dem Acker ein Einkommen haben, damit er nicht brach liegt.

rationale: Thin Infectum 1; plural agent and shared object suffixes across the cultivation sequence.

after: zum ersten Mal ackern, das erste Durchackern ausführen;
rationale: JTM 1.1/3,42 contrast krw with second and fine ploughing; existing Infinitiv already means the first pass. Clarify the agricultural specialization of ackern, without adding or renumbering a sense.

summary: New idiom: babi krule w lə=ṯnele 'keinen zweiten Schlag führen'

data.headword: babi krule w lə=ṯnele 'keinen zweiten Schlag führen'
data.turoyo: Aḥuno, babi krule w lo ṯnele, bu qarʕayḏux, bu ḥalano gṭorenux.
data.translation: Mein Vater hat nur einmal geackert, nicht zweimal. Ich werde dich so mit deinem Kopfe in diesem Zustand lassen.

rationale: Already quoted as literal co-text under krw and ṯny Preterit, but not in either idiom list. The decapitation dialogue establishes proverbial refusal of a second blow; add its pragmatic function with one full context, not a general strike sense.

summary: krw denotes the first cultivation pass in contrast to ṯny and the fine-ploughing verb; coordinated clauses share their field object. The inherited bare ackern is clarified rather than split into a new technical sense.
Infectum Kkoru has an overt field theme; kkurwənne has a suffix-coded theme. The Infinitiv krowo is a complement of finish, not an extra finite occurrence.
The 96/153 proverb is already the sole Preterit example and also appears under ṯny. Allowed searches found no listed idiom, so only an idiom-level contextual annotation is added.
There is no transitive strike sense supported for krw itself. The combat application is conveyed by the whole once-not-twice proverb.
Infectum-wa kərwiwola adds past repeated cultivation to the paradigm already exemplified by Infectum and Infinitiv in round 1. The explicit land noun is resumed by -la.

Jan 1.50/2307 has no -la and no local i arʕo; the reader’s identical arguments for both tokens are not accepted. The interrupted account follows threshing, so its exact agricultural operation is not inferred from the MT alone.

Jan English is project machine translation and does not explicitly say first pass. The first-pass analysis follows the Turoyo contrast with ṯny and the prior entry; its English wording is preserved verbatim.

Do speakers use krw only for the first pass or also generically for ploughing outside these described sequences? The current refinement follows both the supplied sequences and inherited Infinitiv gloss.
Is the 96/153 proverb conventional specifically in refusing a second blow, or does it have a wider once-is-enough pragmatic use? Only the attested combat use is stated.
At Jan 1.50/2307, what are the referents of hno and bəṯru, and does kərwiwo refer to ploughing with an implement or another operation following threshing? The verse does not establish a second sense.
Jan again contrasts krw with second cultivation ṯny, corroborating the round 1 first-pass clarification without another gloss change.
